refs.quote: CIPRO is a fluoroquinolone antibacterial indicated in adults (18 years of age and older) with the following infections caused by designated, susceptible bacteria and in pediatric patients where indicated:

tall_man.note: Not listed in FDA/ISMP Tall Man list; generic name lowercase per EXTRACTION.md

mechanism_of_action.value: Fluoroquinolone bactericidal antibacterial that inhibits bacterial topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV, which are required for bacterial DNA replication, transcription, repair, and recombination.

refs.quote: The bactericidal action of ciprofloxacin results from inhibition of the enzymes topoisomerase II (DNA gyrase) and topoisomerase IV (both Type II topoisomerases), which are required for bacterial DNA replication, transcription, repair, and recombination.

Ciprofloxacin is an inhibitor of human cytochrome P450 1A2 (CYP1A2) mediated metabolism. Co-administration of CIPRO with other drugs primarily metabolized by CYP1A2 results in increased plasma concentrations of these drugs and could lead to clinically significant adverse events of the co-administered drug.

value.effect: Tizanidine Cmax increased 7-fold and AUC increased 10-fold via CYP1A2 inhibition, potentiating hypotensive and sedative effects.
value.management: Concomitant administration of tizanidine and CIPRO is contraindicated.

refs.quote: Tizanidine Contraindicated Concomitant administration of tizanidine and CIPRO is contraindicated due to the potentiation of hypotensive and sedative effects of tizanidine

value.effect: Plasma exposure likely to be increased and prolonged, resulting in increased risk of CNS or other serious/fatal adverse reactions.
value.management: Avoid concomitant use; if unavoidable, monitor serum theophylline levels and adjust dosage as appropriate.

refs.quote: Theophylline Avoid Use (Plasma Exposure Likely to be Increased and Prolonged) Concurrent administration of CIPRO with theophylline may result in increased risk of a patient developing central nervous system (CNS) or other adverse reactions. If concomitant use cannot be avoided, monitor serum levels of theophylline and adjust dosage as appropriate

value.drug_or_class: Drugs Known to Prolong QT Interval (Class IA/III antiarrhythmics, TCAs, macrolides, antipsychotics)
value.effect: CIPRO may further prolong the QT interval in patients receiving QT-prolonging drugs.

refs.quote: Drugs Known to Prolong QT Interval Avoid Use CIPRO may further prolong the QT interval in patients receiving drugs known to prolong the QT interval (for example, class IA or III antiarrhythmics, tricyclic antidepressants, macrolides, antipsychotics)

value.effect: Potential 5-fold increase in duloxetine exposure via CYP1A2 inhibition.
value.management: Avoid use; if unavoidable, monitor for duloxetine toxicity.

value.management: Avoid use; concurrent use is not recommended.

refs.quote: Zolpidem Avoid Use Co-administration with ciprofloxacin may increase blood levels of zolpidem, concurrent use is not recommended

value.drug_or_class: Oral Antidiabetic Drugs (e.g., Sulfonylureas: glyburide, glimepiride)
value.effect: Glucose-lowering effect potentiated; severe hypoglycemia, including fatalities, has been reported.
value.management: Use with caution and monitor blood glucose closely when co-administered.

refs.quote: Hypoglycemia sometimes severe has been reported when CIPRO and oral antidiabetic agents, mainly sulfonylureas (for example, glyburide, glimepiride), were co-administered, presumably by intensifying the action of the oral antidiabetic agent. Fatalities have been reported . Monitor blood glucose when CIPRO is co-administered with oral antidiabetic drugs

value.effect: Altered serum levels of phenytoin (increased and decreased).
value.management: Use with caution; monitor phenytoin serum concentrations during and shortly after co-administration to avoid loss of seizure control or toxicity.

refs.quote: To avoid the loss of seizure control associated with decreased phenytoin levels and to prevent phenytoin overdose-related adverse reactions upon CIPRO discontinuation in patients receiving both agents, monitor phenytoin therapy, including phenytoin serum concentration during and shortly after co-administration of CIPRO with phenytoin.

value.effect: Enhances oral anticoagulant effect (increased INR/prothrombin time).
value.management: Use with caution; monitor prothrombin time, INR, and bleeding frequently during and shortly after co-administration.

refs.quote: Monitor prothrombin time and INR frequently during and shortly after co-administration of CIPRO with an oral anti-coagulant (for example, warfarin).

value.effect: Ropinirole Cmax and AUC increased by 60% and 84%, respectively, via CYP1A2 inhibition.
value.management: Use with caution; monitor for ropinirole-related adverse reactions and adjust ropinirole dose as appropriate.

refs.quote: Ropinirole Use with caution Monitoring for ropinirole-related adverse reactions and appropriate dose adjustment of ropinirole is recommended during and shortly after co-administration with CIPRO

value.effect: Serum concentrations of clozapine and N-desmethylclozapine increased by 29% and 31%, respectively.
value.management: Use with caution; monitor for clozapine adverse reactions and adjust clozapine dose during and shortly after co-administration.

refs.quote: Clozapine Use with caution Careful monitoring of clozapine associated adverse reactions and appropriate adjustment of clozapine dosage during and shortly after co-administration with CIPRO are advised.

tier.note: PLLR Pregnancy section: prospective observational studies (n=200 and n=549 fluoroquinolone exposures) have not identified increased risk of major birth defects or miscarriage, and animal organogenesis studies (mice/rats up to 100 mg/kg PO; rabbits up to 30 mg/kg PO or 20 mg/kg IV) showed no fetal malformations; however, human studies have small sample sizes insufficient for definitive conclusions and juvenile animal arthropathy is a known fluoroquinolone risk.

refs.quote: Prolonged experience with ciprofloxacin in pregnant women over several decades, based on available published information from case reports, case control studies and observational studies on ciprofloxacin administered during pregnancy, have not identified any drug-associated risk of major birth defects, miscarriage or adverse maternal or fetal outcomes (see Data) .

However, these small postmarketing epidemiology studies, of which most experience is from short term, first trimester exposure, are insufficient to evaluate the risk for less common defects or to permit reliable and definitive conclusions regarding the safety of ciprofloxacin in pregnant women and their developing fetuses.

contraception.value: Does not reduce systemic hormonal contraceptive levels; use barrier backup only if severe antibiotic-associated vomiting or diarrhea impairs absorption.
